messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with shortness of breath, dry coughing and fever, after testing positive for COVID-19. The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation, as he had severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. 
Throughout his 31-day hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The chest X-ray revealed bilateral pneumothoraces, which were confirmed with a chest CT, along with pneumomediastinum. The patient was transferred to a hospital where thoracic surgery was available. Imaging after transfer showed that the pneumothorax had slightly increased without tension physiology. The PEEP was decreased from 8 to 6 cm H20 where it remained till his discharge. On the 31st day of admission the patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation. 

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with COVID-19 and developed severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. Throughout his hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, ARDS, volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure on hospital day 31.

Outcome:
The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure after a prolonged hospital stay. 

Follow-Up:
N/A

N/A

N/A

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is COVID-19 with severe pneumonia and respiratory failure, which led to ARDS and the later complications. In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded in chapter U, with U07.1 for virus identified. The three-character category is U07.

CODE: U07
